subject: prd/impl-review
statement: the merge lane's classifier and floor are untouched by impl-review, which adds no lane-side risk logic; the reviewer EMITS a well-formed downgrade signal (the persisted verdict) — the lane's CONSUMPTION of that signal is an owed separate merge-lane amendment (a `Downgrader` adapter that reads the verdict), not the existing GATE-4 slot today
rationale: AP-11 — one risk predicate; impl-review reads the lane's risk classes and emits a downgrade signal, it does not redesign the lane. The base NR-4 overstated "the existing slot consumes it": merge-lane's `Downgrader` seam is synchronous, diff-only, and nil-by-default, so end-to-end lane-forcing requires the owed adapter (design:impl-review-v1#3.6, §7 Q4; the codegate-NR-2 corrective precedent)
fit_criterion: zero impl-review-side diff to the merge lane's classifier or floor (inspection); the persisted verdict validates as a well-formed downgrade signal a lane adapter can read; the consuming `Downgrader` adapter is named owed work (design:impl-review-v1 §7 Q4), gated before adoption relies on lane-forcing — never asserted as an existing consumption
